rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis describes a tribo-corrosion study of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 versus DS2205 after thermal cycling, while the target paper synthesized WTaTiVZr and compared its compression, indentation, and scratch behavior against pure tungsten. These are entirely different kinds of studies (tribo-corrosion vs. mechanical testing of a refractory HEA), so the intervention is a different kind.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses immersed reciprocating sliding in deionized water at 25–100 °C with an alumina ball, whereas the target paper used room-temperature compression, indentation plastometry from RT to 500 °C, and scratch testing with a diamond stylus. The conditions share no regime overlap.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes temperature-dependent depassivation/repassivation, tribo-layer stability, and abrasion/corrosion competition, while the target paper attributes behavior to solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and dislocation-mediated plasticity/toughness improvements. These are completely different classes of mechanism (tribo-corrosion vs. mechanical strengthening and damage tolerance).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower friction, smaller wear volume, and minimized degradation near 50 °C relative to DS2205, whereas the target paper predicts higher strength, greater plasticity, lower BDTT, less scratch damage, and higher fracture toughness relative to pure tungsten. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
